children: shares rose 1.57% to $120.56 at 9:50 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 17, after fiscal fourth-quarter results showed streaming operating income more than doubling. Revenue climbed 16% to $25.9 billion in the quarter ended October 3, helped by an extra week worth about $1.6 billion.

Streaming operating income reached $824 million versus $402 million a year earlier, and Experiences operating income rose 20% to $2.3 billion. Adjusted EPS of $1.77 beat the $1.68 consensus, Yahoo Finance reported in its morning coverage. For fiscal 2027 Disney guided to double-digit adjusted EPS growth, $9 billion of buybacks, $11 billion of free cash flow and nearly $26 billion of content spending. It also set a $3 billion cost savings target by fiscal 2029.

The $9 billion buyback equals about 4.3% of Disney's $208 billion market value, and the free cash flow target covers it with room left for dividends. Hulu's full integration into Disney+ in December will end separate reporting of subscription streaming profit, so the segment gets harder to track next year. GuruFocus gives Disney a GF Score of 87/100, with solid profitability and strong momentum. Its GF Value of $118.65 sits about 2% below the price, a fairly valued reading, so further gains depend on Disney delivering that double-digit growth. The next test is fiscal first-quarter results early next year.

title: Disney Stocks Rise 1.57% as Streaming Profit Doubles and Buybacks Reach $9 Billion
